storyboard.addedInformation: The sprained ankle in the rain names the adversity the callout generalizes.

storyboard.claim: Unspent money goes to a probate lawyer and generates zero stories.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A will-and-estate paper beside a slumped saver clutching his wallet — the inheritance that became paperwork.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast to the ankle story: flawed experience beats untouched money.

storyboard.addedInformation: The clock makes the closing window literal and physical.
storyboard.claim: Money must be converted into memory before the biological window closes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ticking clock over a closing window of healthy years — convert money into memory now.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names the objection out loud instead of illustrating luxury — the staging is the debate itself.

storyboard.concreteVisual: Two people mid-debate at a cafe table — luxury trips and sabbaticals on trial.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the elephant-in-the-room counterpoint after the audacity pitch.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: staging only, the sentence is an incomplete bridge into the privilege question.
storyboard.claim: The hosts ask whether this philosophy applies beyond the wealthy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The questioning host leans in mid-sentence — the applicability challenge, unfinished.

storyboard.concreteVisual: A stack of surplus coins beside the drawdown curve — a framework that assumes you have extra.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens the cafe question into the charge: this caters to the rich.

storyboard.addedInformation: The thin wallet and the suburban street ground the median-earner case without staging the child's condition.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Grounds the privilege charge in concrete cases: the $50k earner, the disabled child.

storyboard.claim: Supporting broke parents in your 40s tests whether audacious spending survives real adversity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A middle-aged earner alone at the table with two stacks of bills, his own and his parents: the wallet stretched between generations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the hardship cases from children to parents going broke.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins on screen concedes the boundary of his own framework.
storyboard.claim: Perkins concedes: if you are paycheck to paycheck, survival is the sole focus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stretched paycheck in coins on a kitchen counter while Perkins acknowledges the survival case.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Perkins answers the hardship cases with an honest exemption.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing gesture ranks needs base-first instead of diagramming a pyramid.
storyboard.claim: The hierarchy of needs demands securing your base first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host ranks needs from the ground up — base secured before anything audacious.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the survival exemption its principle: base before audacity.

storyboard.claim: Audacious decumulation is not for the survival season — but the middle asks what about them.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the exemption and pivots to people with some discretionary income.

storyboard.addedInformation: The gravestone is the certainty; the feared ruin is only a risk — the visual weighs them.
storyboard.claim: Culture overrates the risk of ruin against the biological certainty of death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gravestone on a dusk hill — death certain, ruin merely feared.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The synthesis after the exemption: fear of ruin versus certainty of the grave.

storyboard.addedInformation: The wallet held open is the deliberate choice replacing inertia.
storyboard.claim: Even $10,000 in discretionary savings must be deliberately spent to maximize life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An ordinary saver holds open a wallet of discretionary savings — ten thousand dollars awaiting a decision.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the synthesis to the non-billionaire with savings sitting idle.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck phrase is the rejected behavior; the frozen posture shows it.
storyboard.claim: Letting savings sit out of blind inertia and fear is the rejected default.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A saver stepping forward, savings in motion: inertia broken, fear walked past.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Strikes the behavior beat 252's choice replaces.

storyboard.addedInformation: The open highway is the $10,000 road trip; the dividend math is identical at any price.
storyboard.claim: Road trip or villa, the memory-dividend math of the closing window is identical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A traveler walking an open highway — the cross-country trip whose dividends match the villa's.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Proves the principle scales: $10k trip and $100k villa share one math.

storyboard.addedInformation: The bulb is the rewiring itself — a new idea about money, read literally as insight.
storyboard.claim: The hosts begin the recap: this is a complete rewiring of money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bright bulb over the hosts — the paradigm shift clicking on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the full recap after the scaling proof.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck goal is the autopsy verdict: peak net worth at death equals peak wasted life.
storyboard.claim: Optimizing for maximum net worth at death optimizes for maximum wasted life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A slumped rich corpse beside a struck peak-balance marker — the autopsy of maximum net worth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recap begins at the start: the rich corpse from beat one.

storyboard.addedInformation: The falling dominoes are dividends compounding across the mapped time buckets.
storyboard.claim: Memory dividends compound when experiences are mapped to physical time buckets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock face mapped with time buckets, the drawdown curve falling toward zero.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the recap: dividends, buckets, and the drawdown hurdle.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck coins are the bank balance wealth is NOT; the thinking face weighs the redefinition.
storyboard.claim: Wealth is not what you die with in your bank account.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A saver studies struck coins in a balance display — the rejected definition of wealth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The takeaway stated as negation: wealth is not the balance.

storyboard.addedInformation: The photos are the converted memories; the hourglass is the body that once set the exchange rate.
storyboard.claim: Zero dollars with a full ledger of memory dividends beats riches never spent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A celebrant holds photos of lived experiences under a spent hourglass — the full ledger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The positive half of the definition: what wealth actually is.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slump is the quiet admission; the struck riches are the rejected path.
storyboard.claim: Dying incredibly rich can mean never really spending your life at all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A slumped figure on a cemetery hill beside struck riches — the life never spent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tragic alternative to the full ledger: riches with no life.

storyboard.addedInformation: The close challenge turns the bank balance into a named dream awaiting permission.
storyboard.claim: The challenge: name the dollar amount in your account that is really a dream.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The saver opening his wallet in medium shot: a dream and a trip folded inside the bills.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The recap becomes a direct challenge to the viewer's own account.

storyboard.addedInformation: The reaching gesture is the permission granted — toward the passion project, not just money.
storyboard.claim: Give yourself permission today to live the passion project.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A listener reaches for a long-shelved passion project as the host urges permission now.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the challenge: the permission you were waiting for is yours to give.

storyboard.addedInformation: The ticking clock over the cemetery closes the video where its moral lives.
storyboard.claim: The clock is ticking and the cemetery takes nothing with you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ticking clock over the dusk cemetery hill — time expiring on unspent life.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Final urgency after the permission: why today and not someday.
